blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Event cameras capture asynchronous brightness changes at high temporal resolution, but scarce recordings constrain data-driven research. Sparse RGB observations cannot uniquely determine intervening events since identical frames may correspond to streams with different activity, polarities, and timing. Existing simulators largely rely on prescribed sensor dynamics and estimated brightness trajectories, whose assumptions limit the diversity and fidelity of plausible event streams. We introduce EventDiffusion, a hierarchical generative framework that directly learns the conditional distribution of native asynchronous event streams from real recordings. EventDiffusion decomposes generation into three probabilistic processes: Event Activity Diffusion (EAD) learns stochastic discrete event counts; Event Spatial Allocation (ESA) distributes these counts to individual pixels while preserving cardinality; and Event Timing Diffusion (ETD) learns continuous asynchronous timestamp distributions. We also introduce CEFS, an event-stream realism metric combining event activity and polarity with multiscale space-time structure and temporal fidelity. Across all datasets, EventDiffusion achieves double the accuracy of SOTA methods and demonstrates robustness across different cameras at any resolution.
blocks.zh: 事件相机在高时间分辨度时捕捉出同步亮度变化,但稀缺的录音会制约由数据驱动的研究. Sparse RGB 观测无法独一地决定干涉事件,因为相同的框架可能与具有不同活性,极性,和时间的流相对应. 现有的模拟器主要依靠规定的传感器动力学和估计亮度轨迹,其假设限制了可信事件流的多样性和忠诚性. 我们引入了EventDifmusion, 一个分层基因框架, 直接学习本地同步事件流的有条件分布 从真实的录音。 事件分解将生成分解为三个概率过程: 事件活动扩散(EAD) 学习有条理的离散事件计数; 事件空间分配(ESA) 将这些计数分给单个像素,同时保留基本性; 事件时间扩散(ETD) 学习连续同步时间戳分布. 我们还介绍了CEFS,这是一个事件流现实主义的衡量标准,将事件活动和极性与多尺度的时空结构和时间忠贞性结合起来。 在所有数据集中,EventDifmation使SOTA方法的精度翻了一番,并在任何分辨率上显示不同相机之间的强性.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Event cameras asynchronously report local log-intensity changes exceeding a contrast threshold.
Their microsecond-scale temporal resolution and high dynamic range suit fast motion and challenging illumination [ 4 ] .
However, acquiring large, synchronized RGB-event datasets is costly, motivating realistic event simulation.
blocks.zh:
事件摄像头同步报告本地日志强度变化超过对比阈值。
它们的微秒时间分辨率和高动态射程适合快速运动并具有挑战性照明[4].
然而,获取大型,同步的RGB事件数据集成本高昂,激发现实事件模拟.

blocks.en:
Generating events from sparse RGB observations is fundamentally underdetermined.
Distinct unobserved motion and visibility trajectories can produce identical frames but different event activity, polarities, and timestamps.
Existing simulators address this ambiguity through prescribed sensor dynamics, interpolated or reconstructed brightness trajectories, and learned aggregated event representations [ 24 , 12 , 18 , 37 , 30 ] .
While pragmatic, these assumptions are often too simplistic for real scenes, making sim-to-real transfer challenging.

不同的无观测运动和能见度轨迹可以产生相同的帧但不同的事件活动,极性和时间戳.
现有的模拟器通过规定的传感器动力学、插值或重建亮度轨迹以及学到的聚合事件表述[24、12、18、37、30]来解决这一模糊性。
这些假设虽然务实,但对于真实的场景来说往往过于简单化,使得sim-to-real transfer具有挑战性.

blocks.en: This motivates modelling a distribution over event streams rather than committing to a single realization. The same formulation also supports forecasting. Given only past observations, the model must predict not just future event activity, but also where events occur and when they fire, without access to future RGB frames.
blocks.zh: 这激发了对事件流的分布进行建模,而不是致力于单一实现。 同样的配方也支持预测. 仅考虑到过去的观测结果,模型不仅必须预测未来的事件活动,而且还必须预测事件的发生地点和发射时间,不能访问未来的RGB帧.

blocks.en:
To this end, we introduce EventDiffusion, a hierarchical generative framework that learns a conditional distribution over native asynchronous events from paired RGB and event-camera recordings.
Event generation involves predicting discrete event activity, allocating it across sensor pixels, and modelling continuous firing times. EventDiffusion addresses these through Event Activity Diffusion,
Event Spatial Allocation, and Event Timing Diffusion, respectively. This factorization preserves event counts and polarities while learning the spatial and temporal distributions of individual measurements.
Our approach also allows us to forecast complete asynchronous event streams directly from a single RGB image. Rather than predicting a future event frame or binned representation, it samples individual events and timestamps, allowing the same forecast to be examined at different temporal resolutions.
Evaluating event streams requires measuring activity and timing as well as spatial structure. PECS [ 10 ] can overlook excess events near real ones, while EQS [ 1 ] is insensitive to some count errors. For example, an empty output receives an EQS of 0.94 0.94 or higher, despite missing all real activity. We introduce CEFS, a decomposable metric that compares count, polarity, space-time allocation, and timing against a paired recording. It provides a common evaluation for EventDiffusion and both learned and physics-based simulators.
We evaluate EventDiffusion under native and sparsely sampled RGB inputs, against simulators that also receive interpolated frames. Our experiments assess event fidelity, temporal statistics, and generalization across DSEC [ 8 ] , EDS [ 11 ] , BS-ERGB [ 32 ] , and CEAR [ 40 ] .
We also evaluate forecasting against real future event streams.
Our contributions are: 1. The first learned diffusion model of the RGB-conditioned distribution over asynchronous event streams. 2. A hierarchical generation approach that models integer event counts, allocates them to pixels while preserving their totals, and generates continuous timestamps. 3. Causal Forecasting of native asynchronous event streams, generating individual future events and their timestamps without access to future RGB observations. 4. CEFS, a decomposable,
multiscale metric of event count, polarity,
spatial, temporal, and joint space–time fidelity.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Reconstruction-Based Event Simulation
blocks.zh: 2.1 基于重建的活动模拟

blocks.en:
Many event simulators apply explicit sensor-response models to brightness trajectories. ESIM [ 24 ] samples scene intensity through motion-adaptive rendering. For recorded video, VID2E [ 6 ] interpolates intermediate RGB frames before simulation, but its events depend on the interpolation quality and a single interpretation of the unobserved scene.
Subsequent methods refine the sensor response to a
supplied brightness trajectory.
v2e [ 12 ] incorporates finite bandwidth, threshold variation, leakage, and noise, while DVS-Voltmeter [ 18 ] models stochastic pixel-voltage dynamics.
Characterization-based simulators [ 15 ] incorporate measured hardware behaviour, and SENPI [ 9 ] provides a differentiable sensor simulation framework.
FracEvent [ 3 ] further models fractional-relaxation voltage dynamics with retained pixel memory and continuous threshold-crossing times.
These approaches improve sensor realism and temporal fidelity.
Scene-based methods improve the underlying brightness trajectory. PECS [ 10 ] models optical and multispectral image formation from 3D scenes, while TIDES [ 30 ] reconstructs dynamic Gaussian scenes to derive continuous-time intensity changes with visibility and sensor readout effects. Both rely on a specified or reconstructed scene and sensor response. EventDiffusion instead learns event-stream distributions from paired observations without scene reconstruction or intermediate brightness trajectories.

blocks.en: 2.2 Learned Event Representations
blocks.zh: 2.2 总结经验

blocks.en: Learning-based methods differ in their output representations. EventGAN [ 39 ] learns image-conditioned event volumes using adversarial and consistency losses. V2CE [ 37 ] synthesizes event voxels before recovering continuous timestamps, while V2V [ 19 ] generates compact voxels for efficient storage and training.
blocks.zh: 基于学习的方法在产出表述上有所不同。 EventGAN [39] 利用对抗性和一致性损失来学习图像化事件卷. V2CE [37]在恢复连续时间戳前合成事件 voxel,而 V2V [19] 生成紧凑的 voxel,用于高效的存储和训练.

blocks.en: Other generative methods broaden the conditioning modalities. Text-to-Events [ 23 ] combines diffusion with an event-frame autoencoder, while ControlEvents [ 13 ] transfers image-diffusion priors to semantic and pose conditioning. Both use temporally aggregated representations. Texvent [ 33 ] generates video before interpolation and physics-based simulation to produce asynchronous events. These methods do not learn event timing conditioned on allocated event marks.
blocks.zh: 其他基因方法拓宽了条件模式. Text-to-Events [23] 将扩散与事件帧自动编码器结合,而ControlEvents [13] 将图像扩散前缀转移至语义化和姿势化. 两者都使用时间上的汇总表述. Texvent [33] 在插值和物理模拟之前生成视频,以产生同步事件. 这些方法不学习以分配的事件标记为条件的事件时间安排。

blocks.en:
Diffusion has also been applied directly to event
clouds, albeit under different generation objectives.
Zhang et al. [ 36 ] formulate sparse event completion as diffusion-based
spatiotemporal point-cloud refinement, reconstructing
missing events from partial recordings.
Unlike RGB-conditioned simulation, this setting
assumes observed event measurements and targets
recovery of an incomplete event stream.
More generally, Point Set Diffusion [ 20 ] models random finite
point sets through thinning and noise superposition,
supporting variable-cardinality generation.
CountsDiff [ 27 ] develops
diffusion processes on the natural numbers for
discrete count distributions.
Event-camera simulation requires integrating these mechanisms with polarity-aware activity, count-conserving spatial allocation, and fine-grained temporal dependencies. EventDiffusion addresses these coupled requirements through a hierarchical event-specific generative model.

Event forecasting predicts future event measurements from past observations.
E-Motion [ 35 ] adapts video diffusion to forecast future event representations from event history.
E-TIDE [ 26 ] instead uses a lightweight deterministic network to predict temporally binned, polarity-separated event occurrence maps.
These approaches forecast aggregated representations, whereas EventDiffusion generates individual events with locations, polarities, and timestamps.

这些方法预测了综合表述,而事件传播则产生有地点、极性和时间戳的个别事件。

blocks.en: 2.3 Measuring Asynchronous Event Fidelity
blocks.zh: 2.3 同步测量 事件

blocks.en:
PECS [ 10 ] compares events in space, time, and polarity using Chamfer and Gaussian distances. Its many-to-one matching can mask timing, count, and structural errors. EQS [ 1 ] compares event-trained transformer features but depends on temporally aggregated inputs. TIDES [ 30 ] adds timestamp-artifact diagnostics.
No prior work has proposed a unified criterion covering all aspects of event realism.
We introduce CEFS to evaluate these aspects of event fidelity, using reference-derived scale weights to reduce the influence of unreliable resolutions.
blocks.zh:
PECS [10] 利用Chamfer和Gaussian的距离来比较空间,时间和极度上的事件. 它的多对一匹配可以掩盖时机,计数和结构错误. EQS [1] 比较事件训练变压器的特性,但取决于时间上的汇总输入. TIDES [30] 添加时间戳-艺术诊断.
以前的工作没有提出涵盖事件现实主义各个方面的统一标准。
我们采用CEFS来评价事件忠贞的这些方面,利用参考推算的尺度权重来减少不可靠分辨率的影响。

blocks.en:
ESA defines where events occur spatially, but their temporal distribution is still highly complex. To ensure that we can model the refractory period, burstiness, and other quirks of
real event streams, we learn a joint distribution of all the event timestamps within a spatial patch and slice. Learning this joint distribution in one pass is hard, because each event’s plausible times depend on the times of the others. Instead, we corrupt the timestamps step by step towards uniform noise and learn to reverse the corruption. At each reverse step, the model decides which events already hold plausible times, keeps them, and redraws the rest. Constraints between events, such as a refractory gap after a pixel’s last event, are then imposed against events already in place.

blocks.en: 4 Measuring Event-Stream Fidelity
blocks.zh: 4 衡量事件 -- -- 结构化

blocks.en: Event-stream fidelity depends jointly on activity, polarity, spatial structure, and timing, regardless of how the stream is generated. As discussed in Sec. 2 , existing geometric and feature-based metrics capture complementary aspects of this fidelity. We introduce the Composite Event Fidelity Score (CEFS) to evaluate these properties together while retaining interpretable components.
blocks.zh: 事件流的忠贞性共同取决于活动、极性、空间结构和时间,而不论流是如何产生的。 如第2节所述,现有的几何测量和基于特征的测量方法涵盖了这种忠诚的互补方面。 我们采用综合事件Fidelity评分(CEFS)来评估这些属性,同时保留可解释的组成部分。

blocks.en: CEFS compares generated events with a paired real recording over the same interval and sensor area, without count matching or realignment. Let g g and r r index the generated and recorded streams, respectively, as used in the component definitions below. CEFS requires no trained network or fitting to generated events. Scale weights depend only on the recording, and the two coefficients are fixed using corrupted real recordings (supplement). blocks.en: 5.1 Experimental Settings

blocks.en:
We evaluate test sets in DSEC [ 8 ] , EDS [ 11 ] ,
BS-ERGB [ 32 ] , and CEAR [ 40 ] with recording-level splits. All the baselines are calibrated separately for each dataset.
We evaluate two versions of EventDiffusion. In EventDiffusion-G, each of EAD, ESA and ETD is a single checkpoint shared by all datasets and, in EventDiffusion-FT, all three are fine-tuned for each dataset.
All methods in the simulation experiments use only RGB frames as inputs.
We compare Native RGB frames, SSM-10 × \times (the same frames plus fixed 10 × 10\times Super SloMo [ 14 ] interpolation), and
Gap-5 × \times (every fifth native frame) on identical reference-event
windows. Preprocessing, dataset eligibility, and input requirements are in
the supplement. We report CEFS (Sec. 4 ), EQS [ 1 ] , and
PECS distances, alongside temporal diagnostics; full metric definitions are in
the supplement.
CEFS uses spatial bin sizes of { 1 , 2 , 4 , 8 , 16 } \{1,2,4,8,16\} px and temporal bin sizes of { 10 , 50 , 100 , 500 } ​ μ \{10,50,100,500\}\,\mu s and { 1 , 5 } \{1,5\} ms (30 combinations).
Unless stated otherwise, scores are computed on the test windows
over complete valid 32 × 32 32{\times}32 px patches. Each sequence is averaged over
its windows, then each dataset is averaged over its sequences. In the result
tables, red, orange and yellow cells mark
the first, second and third best result in each column.
All models are trained on a single NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU
using Adam for 100K iterations each.
EAD, ESA, and ETD are trained independently using their
respective objectives, with self-conditioning fine-tuning
to mitigate exposure bias.
Further implementation details are provided in the supplementary material.

blocks.en:
Table 5 groups the comparisons by input: a single RGB frame, past RGB frames, and event history. For event history, we compare against E-Motion [ 35 ] , which conditions on event-voxel frames, using its released checkpoint. For the RGB-prediction-plus-simulation baselines, SimVP [ 5 , 29 ] forecasts the future RGB frames from the two latest observed frames, which are then passed to an event simulator. We also report Cosmos Edge [ 22 ] as the video predictor, but it takes
5 RGB frames as input to generate the future frames.
CEFS applies only to native event streams, so E-Motion’s voxel forecasts are scored with mIoU and F1 against the ground truth only. The evaluation procedure is detailed in the supplementary material.
EventDiffusion achieves the strongest performance in every comparison, including with only a single RGB frame or only past events as input. Voxel predictors such as E-Motion use fixed temporal aggregation, while RGB-prediction-plus-simulation pipelines depend on an estimated future brightness trajectory.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
EventDiffusion generates and causally forecasts native asynchronous event streams through three stages that model activity, spatial allocation, and continuous timing. This factorization makes their assumptions independently testable.
Future work could explore forecasting as a step towards predictive world models operating directly on asynchronous sensor measurements.

今后的工作可以探索预测,以此作为直接在同步传感器测量上运作的预测世界模型的一个步骤。

This gives 240 DSEC, 120 EDS, 525 BS-ERGB and 960 CEAR windows. SSM-10 × \times and Gap-5 × \times outputs are scored on the same native intervals.

We compare ESIM [ 24 ] , v2e [ 12 ] , IEBCS [ 15 ] , DVS-Voltmeter [ 18 ] , V2CE [ 37 ] and FracEvent [ 3 ] in Tables 1–3 of the main paper.
For each simulator, we calibrate their parameters. V2CE is fine-tuned on each dataset at its native resolution from the released checkpoint.

我们比较了ESIM [24],v2e [12],IEBCS [15],DVS-Voltmeter [18],V2CE [37]和FracEvent [3]在主论文表1-3中.
对于每个模拟器, 我们校准它们的参数。 V2CE从已放行的检查站根据其原生分辨率对每个数据集进行微调.

Gap-5 × \times retains every fifth native RGB frame, so each gap [ t k , t k + 5 ) [t_{k},t_{k+5}) receives only its two end frames, while the reference event stream and the scored windows stay fixed.
blocks.zh: 原生 RGB 在录制时使用录制的帧, 在每录制帧 - 事件抵消 Sec. A.2 之后。 SSM- 10 ×\ 时间添加固定 10 × 10\ 时间 Super SloMo内插[14]. Gap-5×\times保留了每五分之一的原生RGB帧,因此每个漏洞[t k,t k + 5][t_{k},t_{k+5}]只收到其两个端帧,而参考事件流和得分窗口保持固定.

blocks.en: A.2 Preprocessing and Dataset Fixes
blocks.zh: A.2 预处理和数据集

blocks.en: Events stay on each event camera’s own pixel grid, and the RGB frames are resampled onto that grid. Each dataset also gives a mask of the pixels where both events and RGB are valid, and scoring uses only complete valid 32 × 32 32{\times}32 px patches.
blocks.zh: 每个事件相机的像素网格上都保留事件, RGB 帧被重印到该网格上 。 每个数据集还给出了事件和RGB都有效的像素的遮罩,评分只使用完整有效的32×32 32\times}32 px补丁.

blocks.en:
The RGB and event cameras are about 4.4 cm apart, so mapping the frames into the event grid with the calibrated rotation and rectification alone leaves near objects misaligned.
Therefore we use a depth-aware alignment. We estimate metric depth for each RGB frame with MoGe-2 [ 34 ] and, for every event pixel, solve for the RGB pixel that sees the same 3D point, using the calibrated rotation and translation.
Pixels without a depth estimate are treated as far away, surfaces nearer than 1.5 m are sampled at 1.5 m, and pixels hidden from the RGB camera take their appearance from the nearby far side of the occluding edge.
blocks.zh:
RGB和事件相机相距约4.4厘米,因此用校准的旋转和校正将帧映射到事件网格中,单是让物体靠近错位.
因此,我们采用深度意识的组合。 我们用 MoGe-2 [34] 来估计每个 RGB 框架的度量深度,对于每个事件像素,用校准的旋转和翻译来解析看到相同3D点的 RGB 像素.
无深度估计的像素被处理为远方,1.5米以上的表面在1.5米处取样,隐藏在RGB相机上的像素从邻近的远边上取出它们的外观.

blocks.en:
EDS records with a beam splitter, so the RGB frames are mapped into the event grid by a depth-free warp through the release’s calibration.
A per-recording registration correction and a frame–event clock offset are fitted by aligning frames with events, for every recording.
blocks.zh:
EDS记录带有光束分解器,因此RGB帧通过发行的校准通过无深度曲速绘制成事件网格.
每一份记录的登记更正和帧-活动时钟的抵消都通过使帧与事件一致来进行。

blocks.en:
Both releases store events already warped into RGB image coordinates, BS-ERGB on a 1 / 32 1/32 -pixel lattice and HS-ERGB as floating-point positions.
The warp leaves curved lines and lattice points that can never receive an event. For each recording we instead rebuild an integer sensor lattice from the event positions that occur and a fitted coordinate map, and resample the frames onto it.
Events that do not fall on the rebuilt lattice are excluded. HS-ERGB is split into windows by timestamp, and spans where its event stream drops out are excluded.
blocks.zh:
两者都释放已扭曲到RGB图像坐标的存储事件,BS-ERGB在1/32 1/32-像素拉蒂塞和HS-ERGB上作为浮点位置.
曲面留下了永远无法接收到事件的弯曲线条和纹饰点. 每次录制时,我们都会从事件位置重建一个整数传感器网格, 并重新绘制一个座标图, 并重新对框架进行采样。
不落在重建的窗帘上的事件不包括在内。 HS- ERGB 被时间戳分割成窗口, 其事件流退出的跨度被排除在外 。

blocks.en:
CEAR records with two event cameras, a DVXplorer ( 320 × 240 320\times 240 ) and a DAVIS346 ( 346 × 260 346\times 260 ), and a separate RGB camera with depth registered to the event camera.
We read each recording’s event camera from its file header, since the file names do not identify it reliably. The RGB frames are warped into the event grid using the recorded depth (matched in time to each frame) and the calibrated event-to-RGB extrinsics.
Missing depth takes the nearest depth within 6 px and is otherwise treated as far away, and frames with no depth within 20 ms are treated as far. Both cameras’ event-to-RGB extrinsics and every recording’s clock offset are refined by aligning the frames with the events.
blocks.zh:
CEAR记录有两台事件摄像头,一台DVXplorer(320×240 320\times 240)和一台DAVIS346(346×260 346\times 260),另外一台深度登记在事件摄像头上的RGB摄像头.
我们从文件头读到每个记录的事件相机, RGB帧通过记录的深度(与每个帧的时间匹配)和校准的事件到RGB外部线条被扭曲成事件网格.
缺失的深度在6px以内取最接近的深度,否则被处理为远处,20ms以内无深度的帧被处理为远处. 两台相机的相机对RGB的外观和每台录音的时钟偏移都通过将相框与事件对齐来改进.

blocks.en:
EvSLAM records with a stereo pair of event cameras ( 640 × 480 640\times 480 ) and a separate RGB camera, on two rigs with different RGB–event extrinsics. One recording without RGB frames is excluded.
The dataset’s depth images are not metric, so, as for DSEC, the frames are warped with MoGe-2 depth scaled by a factor fitted per camera set, using the time offsets from a Kalibr calibration and extrinsics refined by aligning frames with events.
The refinement scans include the test recording arm_hdr . The RGB camera sees only part of the event cameras’ field of view, so only the overlap is valid and scored. Some views show black strips or rolling-shutter effects, which we do not correct.
blocks.zh:
EvSLAM用立体对事件摄像头(640×480 640\times 480)和单独的RGB摄像头记录,在两台具有不同RGB-活动外观的钻机上. 一个没有RGB帧的录音被排除在外.
数据集的深度图像不是度量的,因此,至于DSEC, 帧与 MoGe-2 深度相错,每套相机安装一个因数,利用卡利伯校准的时间抵消,并通过将帧与事件对齐而精炼。
精细扫描包括测试录臂_hdr. RGB相机只看到事件相机的部分视场,因此只有重叠才有效并得分. 有些观点显示黑色条纹或滚动-舒特效应,我们对此没有纠正.

blocks.en: A.3 Forecasting Protocol
blocks.zh: A.3 预测协议

blocks.en:
Forecasting is evaluated on BS-ERGB’s 21 scored test recordings (Sec. A.1 ).
Each recording has one forecast origin t 0 t_{0} , the start of the 11th of its 25 test windows, and the forecast covers the five frame intervals that follow, about 187 ms at BS-ERGB’s mean interval of 37.4 ms.
No frame after t 0 t_{0} is given to any method.
blocks.zh:
预测是在BS-ERGB的21个得分测试录音(Sec.A.1)上评价的.
每张录音都有一个预测源 t 0 t_{0}, 开始其25个测试窗口中的第11个, 预测覆盖随后的5个帧间隔,
t0 t_{0} 之后的帧没有给任何方法.

blocks.en: EventDiffusion forecasts by rollout, generating one frame interval at a time in 8 slices, and each later interval reads the stream generated before it as its history. The input settings are: • Single RGB : the frame at t 0 t_{0} , given at every step with its age, and no past events. • RGB + events : the frame at t 0 t_{0} , aged as above, and the real events before t 0 t_{0} . • Past RGB : the events between the two frames before t 0 t_{0} , generated by EventDiffusion from those frames, then the frame at t 0 t_{0} , aged as above. • Past events : the real events before t 0 t_{0} and no frame. EAD reads the last slice of the history and ESA and ETD the last 20 ms, so “Events (20 ms)” in Table 5 of the main paper is the longest span any stage reads. The forecast’s event count is not anchored to the past rate.

blocks.zh: 单 RGB : fram at t 0 t_{0}, 随年龄逐步给出,没有过去的事件.

blocks.en: RGB + events : the frame at t 0 t_{0} , aged as above, and the real events before t 0 t_{0} .

blocks.en: In order to evaluate the baselines fairly, using their own proposed protocols, each one is provided either with equivalent or greater amounts of conditioning evidence to support its forecasts, and we initialise from their pre-trained weights where available. RGB prediction plus simulation. SimVP [ 5 , 29 ] (v2, gSTA) is trained on BS-ERGB’s training recordings to predict five frames from the two latest observed frames. Cosmos Edge [ 22 ] predicts the five frames from the five latest observed frames in one call. ESIM and DVS-Voltmeter then simulate events from the predicted frames with their calibrated BS-ERGB parameters, after warming up on the three latest observed frames. In contrast, our own technique only ever receives 1 or 2 RGB frames. Event history. E-TIDE had no released code or checkpoint to support this comparison. E-Motion [ 35 ] is run on 6 voxel frames at 60 fps, the 100 ms of real events before t 0 t_{0} , with the event camera’s lattice resized to 256 × 256 256\times 256 as its code expects. In contrast, our own technique only ever receives 0 or 20 ms of past events.

blocks.en: Appendix B Method and Implementation Details
blocks.zh: 附录B 方法和实施细节

blocks.en: EventDiffusion generates a native event stream through a sequence of conditional decisions. EAD samples polarity-specific event counts for each spatial cell and time slice. ESA allocates those counts to pixels while preserving their totals. ETD assigns timestamps to the resulting events while retaining their pixels and polarities. Each stage therefore resolves a distinct part of the stream while preserving the decisions made before it. The same factorization supports both generation between RGB frames and forecasting beyond the last observed frame. Secs. B.1 – B.3 give the details of each stage, Sec. B.4 their training, including a few-step version of EAD’s sampler, Sec. B.5 forecasting, and Sec. B.6 the time generation takes.

The RGB frames are encoded using a U-Net whose encoder is BiT’s ResNetV2-50x1 [ 17 ] with ImageNet-21k weights, its first convolution widened to the ten input channels, and whose decoder is FiLM-modulated by the interval’s length and the camera embedding.
It is trained jointly with EAD. Its input is the two RGB frames that bound the interval, their log-luminance images, the absolute difference of the two log-luminances, and a mask of the valid sensor support.

它与高等教育学院共同培训。 它的输入是绑定间隔的两个RGB框架,它们的日志发光图像,两个日志发光的绝对差,以及有效的传感器支持的遮罩.

EAD also takes the history of the previous interval as input.
The event history is the ON and OFF counts of the last slice before the interval, read as log ⁡ ( 1 + n ) / 2 \log(1+n)/2 , with that span’s duration in units of 20 ms.
In training, 30% of intervals keep their real history, so the model also learns to start without one. To reduce exposure bias, training also uses one-frame intervals whose history is the previous interval’s last slice, sampled by an earlier EAD checkpoint in stored chained rollouts over the training sequences.
Each camera has a learned baseline event rate λ d cam \lambda_{d_{\rm cam}} , initialized from the count statistics of the training data, and a learned embedding that enters the network. Index 0 is an unknown camera with its own baseline event rate and embedding. In training, the camera is replaced by the unknown one with probability 0.15, so the model can also generate for a camera it has not seen.

blocks.en: B.2 Event Spatial Allocation
blocks.zh: B.2 事件空间分配

blocks.en:
ESA turns each sampled cell count into pixel-level events through hierarchical splits. Each split assigns m m events to one region and the remaining n − m n-m to the other, preserving the polarity-specific count exactly as spatial detail is introduced. A fully convolutional U-Net predicts the parameters ( η , κ ) (\eta,\kappa) of Eq. (5) of the main paper for every split. It works at resolutions of 1, 2, 4 and 8 pixels with widths 32, 64, 96 and 128, two FiLM residual blocks per level in the encoder and one in the decoder, and its head reads the 1 px features, folded into 2 px cells, together with the 2 px features.
Its inputs are EAD’s ten RGB input channels on the event grid, the cell mask m c m_{c} , each cell’s counts repeated over its pixels, each pixel’s position within its cell, and the pixel counts of the cells already allocated. The event history is, per polarity, log ⁡ ( 1 + n ) \log(1+n) of the counts in the 20 ms before the slice. FiLM conditioning carries the slice’s position and duration, whether frames are given,
and the event history’s duration. In training the event history is absent for 60% of samples, partial for 10% and complete for 30%, and with probability 0.5 it comes from a stored stream generated by the full pipeline.

blocks.en: B.3 Event Timing Diffusion
blocks.zh: B.3 传播时间

blocks.en: ETD models the timing of the events placed by ESA, keeping their number, pixels and polarities fixed. Its conditional density combines a background component for temporal variation, anchor kernels for correlations with nearby events, row and column context for timestamp sharing, and same-pixel inhibition for refractory behaviour. Together these terms place individual events in time while retaining the activity and spatial allocation sampled by the preceding stages.

blocks.en: B.4 Training
blocks.zh: B.4 培训

blocks.en: EAD, ESA, and ETD are trained independently using their respective objectives. Each stage is first trained on the pooled training recordings to produce the shared EventDiffusion-G pipeline. EventDiffusion-FT subsequently fine-tunes the stages on each dataset to adapt to its event statistics. During later training phases, a proportion of batches use event histories generated by an earlier version of the pipeline rather than recorded histories. This reduces the mismatch between training and inference, where each generated interval conditions subsequent generation. Table S2 specifies the optimizer and cumulative training steps for each stage and checkpoint.
blocks.zh: EAD、欧空局和ETD分别根据各自的目标接受独立培训。 每个阶段首先接受集成培训录音培训,以制作共享事件传播-G管道。 EventDifumation-FT随后微调了每个数据集的阶段,以适应其事件统计. 在后来的培训阶段,部分批次使用早先版本的管道生成的事件历史而不是记录的历史。 这减少了训练与推论的不匹配性,在推论中,每一个都产生了后一代的间隔条件. 表S2规定了每个阶段和检查站的优化和累积培训步骤。

blocks.en: Each stage is trained on one GPU with AdamW ( β = ( 0.9 , 0.99 ) \beta=(0.9,0.99) , weight decay 0.01), a linear warm-up followed by cosine decay to 10% of the peak learning rate in every training phase, gradient clipping at 1.0 and bf16 autocast. In half of the batches of the later training phases, the event history each stage reads is generated by an earlier version of the pipeline (Secs. B.1 – B.3 ).

blocks.en: EAD’s iterative reverse process produces the cell counts that determine the number of events ESA must allocate. To reduce the number of network evaluations while preserving this interface, we train a student to take eight larger reverse steps in place of the teacher’s 128. The student retains EAD’s network and the integer-valued update of Eq. ( S1 ), so its sampled ON/OFF counts pass directly to ESA without changing the subsequent stages.

blocks.en: For each training batch, we choose a step i i on the student’s eight-step grid. The student’s moving average samples from an empty map up to that step, exposing training to the count maps the student encounters during generation. From the resulting map, the frozen teacher covers the next student step in four steps of the second-order θ \theta -trapezoidal sampler ( θ = 1 2 \theta=\tfrac{1}{2} ). The training target is the teacher’s expected count addition over those steps, for each cell, polarity and slice. The student predicts a missing count so that its single reverse step matches that target in expectation, using the count error of Eq. (3) of the main paper. The loss matches expected additions, rather than the complete joint distribution of the teacher’s transitions. Each student step remains a product of binomials and produces integer counts. We train the student for 6,000 steps (learning rate 2 × 10 − 5 2\times 10^{-5} after 500 warm-up steps, EMA decay 0.999) on the teacher’s training data, including generated histories.

blocks.en: B.5 Forecasting
blocks.zh: B.5 预测

blocks.en: EventDiffusion forecasts individual asynchronous events, including their pixel locations, polarities, and continuous timestamps, from different combinations of past observations. The same generative framework supports a single RGB frame, multiple past RGB frames, event history alone, or RGB combined with event history. Unlike approaches that predict temporally aggregated event representations, the output is a native event stream whose temporal resolution is not fixed by the forecasting model. Unlike RGB-prediction-plus-simulation approaches, EventDiffusion does not require an intermediate prediction of future RGB frames.
blocks.zh: EventDifusion从过去观测的不同组合中预测单个同步事件,包括其像素位置,极度,以及连续时间戳. 同一个基因框架支持一个单一的RGB框架,多个过去的RGB框架,单独的事件历史,或者RGB与事件历史相结合. 与预测时间总和事件表现的方法不同,输出是原生事件流,其时间分辨率没有被预测模型固定. 与RGB预测-+-模拟方法不同,EventDifmation不需要对未来RGB框架的中间预测.

blocks.en: Forecasting uses the same activity–allocation–timing factorization as RGB-conditioned simulation. Starting from the observations available at the forecast origin, EAD generates future activity, ESA allocates the sampled counts to native sensor pixels, and ETD generates continuous timestamps for those events. Generation proceeds causally, one frame interval at a time in eight temporal slices, with each subsequent interval conditioned on the previously generated events. No future RGB frames are supplied. Section A.3 specifies the conditioning and evaluation for each forecast setting.
blocks.zh: 预测使用与RGB条件模拟相同的活动-分配-定时因子化. 从预测源的观测数据开始,EAD产生未来的活动,欧空局将抽样计数分配给本土传感器像素,ETD为这些事件产生连续的时间戳。 生成因果发生,一次一个帧间隔分8个时间片段,之后的每次间隔都以以前产生的事件为条件. 不提供未来的 RGB 框架 。 A.3节规定了每个预测设置的条件和评价。

blocks.en: Forecasting requires the stages to operate with the observations available at the origin and with their own generated history. During training, the end frame is dropped in 30% of batches, and previous events are dropped in another 30%. The later training phases also use generated histories (Sec. B.4 ). These settings expose the model to the missing-frame and history conditions encountered at inference, while retaining the same three-stage generation process.
blocks.zh: 预测需要各阶段在源头和自身产生的历史中进行观测。 在培训期间,30%的批次降低了终点,另外30%减少了以前的事件。 后期培训阶段还使用了生成的历史(第B.4节)。 这些设置使模型暴露在推断时遇到的缺失框架和历史条件,同时保留了相同的三阶段生成过程.

blocks.en: During a rollout, the history available to EAD changes from an observed event stream to events sampled by the model itself. To make the preparation of this conditioning explicit, the second EAD fine-tuning phase applies Diffusion Forcing [ 2 ] to the sequence of slices and the event history. Its noise process is EAD’s own count thinning (Eq. (1) of the main paper). In half of the gaps, each slice draws its own noise level. In half of the gaps with a history, the history is thinned to a random level and that level is supplied to the network. The model thus learns to predict future activity with context at different known thinning levels.
blocks.zh: 在推出过程中,EAD可用的历史从观测到的事件流变化到模型本身取样的事件. 为了明确这个条件的制备,第二个 EAD 微调阶段对切片的顺序和事件历史应用了扩散强化[2]. 它的噪声过程是EAD自己的计数薄化(主论文Eq. (1)). 在一半的空隙中,每个切片会画出自己的噪音水平. 在有历史的缺口中,有一半的历史被稀疏到一个随机的级别,该级别提供给网络. 因此,该模型学习了在不同已知稀薄水平上预测未来活动。

blocks.en: At inference, an observed event history is supplied unchanged at level 0. A history generated by EventDiffusion is thinned to level 0.5 and supplied with that level. This gives EAD access to previous activity for continuity while distinguishing generated context from an unthinned observation. ESA and ETD then allocate and time the sampled activity as in the rest of the pipeline.
blocks.zh: 推断,观测到的事件历史在水平上没有变化 零点 EventionDifmation生成的历史稀释到0.5级,并以该级供给. 这使EAD能够持续地访问先前的活动,同时区分生成的上下文和未切除的观察. 然后,欧空局和ETD像管道的其余部分一样,对取样活动进行分配和分配时间。

blocks.zh: B.6 推断和运行时间

blocks.en:
Table S3 compares generation time on DSEC with fidelity. We use the distilled EAD with 8 steps (Sec. B.4 ), ESA allocating every cell at once, and ETD with 6 steps. EAD draws the next frame interval while ESA and ETD process the current one, so an interval takes about as long as ETD (4.4 s) rather than the sum of the three stages.
The faster baselines incur a substantial loss in event fidelity. On DSEC, V2CE generates a frame interval in 0.141 s but reaches a CEFS of 0.502, while DVS-Voltmeter takes 1.17 s with interpolated frames and reaches 0.576. EventDiffusion takes 4.8 s per interval and achieves 0.700 using native RGB frames. Its additional computation therefore provides substantially higher measured event fidelity, making it attractive when generation is performed offline and the resulting streams are reused.

blocks.en: C.4 Failure Cases of PECS and EQS
blocks.zh: C.4 PECS和EQS的失败案例

blocks.en:
Existing event-stream metrics capture complementary aspects of
fidelity but can overlook important discrepancies.
blocks.zh:
现有事件流程衡量尺度包括:
忠诚但可以忽略重大差异。

blocks.en:
PECS [ 10 ] independently min–max normalizes
each event stream before computing Chamfer and Gaussian distances.
Consequently, a constant spatial translation or temporal shift
can leave the normalized point sets unchanged, producing zero
distance despite misalignment in the original sensor coordinates.
Nearest-neighbour matching can also overlook duplicated events,
since multiple generated events may match the same reference event.
CEFS instead evaluates streams in their shared physical coordinates
and explicitly penalizes count discrepancies.
blocks.zh:
PECS [10] 独立分钟-最大常态
每个事件流在计算钱弗和高斯距离之前。
因此,恒定空间翻译或时间变化
可将常态点集保留不变,生成零
距离,尽管在原始传感器坐标上出现错位。
近邻匹配也可以忽略重复的事件,
因为多个生成的事件可能匹配相同的引用事件.
CEFS则评价其共享物理坐标中的流
并明确惩罚计数差异。

blocks.en:
EQS [ 1 ] compares learned event representations.
Our evaluation uses a pretrained RVT-Small [ 7 ] encoder with ten temporal count bins. This adaptation can be
insensitive to fine timestamp changes and missing activity.
CEFS directly evaluates event counts, multiscale space–time
structure, and temporal fidelity without relying on a learned
feature representation.
blocks.zh:
EQS [1] 比较学到的事件表述.
我们的评价使用一个预选的 RVT-Small [7] 编码器,有10个时间计数箱. 这种适应可以是
对精细的时间戳变化和缺少活动不敏感。
CEFS 直接评价事件计数, 多尺度时空
结构,和时间忠贞而不依赖知识
特征表示。

blocks.en:
Section G.2 provides controlled comparisons with PECS and EQS,
including absolute-alignment, event-duplication, and timestamp
quantization experiments.

blocks.en: Both tables use EventDiffusion’s RGB + events forecasts of Table 5 of the main paper, from the forecasting model of Sec. B.5 (BS-ERGB, 21 test sequences, five frame intervals from the origin, three seeds). Table S9 isolates timestamp assignment by keeping every event’s pixel, polarity and slice fixed and varying only its time within the slice. ETD lowers burst Fano error to 1.08 1.08 , compared with 1.33 1.33 for uniform times and 1.29 1.29 for a causal per-patch rate. It achieves lower Fano error in 54 and 52 of the 63 sequence–seed pairs, respectively. This improvement is obtained on the same forecast counts and locations, showing that ETD contributes temporal structure beyond the activity and allocation stages.

blocks.en: D.2 Downstream Models Trained on Generated Events
blocks.zh: D.2 下游模式对产生事件的培训

blocks.en:
Table S11 asks whether generated events can replace real recordings as training data. EventDiffusion-FT generates DSEC’s 41 training sequences whole from their RGB frames, each interval following the stream generated before it.
E2VID [ 25 ] is trained from scratch on these events with its authors’ recipe (320k iterations, LPIPS and temporal-consistency losses, the final checkpoint) and scored on the real events of the 12 test recordings against their RGB frames warped onto the event camera.
ESS [ 28 ] trains its segmentation decoder with the authors’ settings on the events of DSEC-Semantic’s 8 training sequences, over a frozen E2VID trained on generated events, and is scored after the 50th epoch on the real events of its 3 test sequences. We train E2VID and ESS in the same way on events generated separately by ESIM, DVS-Voltmeter and V2CE.

blocks.en: E.1 Sampler and Allocation Ablations
blocks.zh: E.1 抽样和分配

blocks.en:
These ablations vary one stage at a time around a few-step version of EventDiffusion-FT on DSEC test. Table S14 samples EAD at 2 to 32 steps, with ESA and ETD fixed. Table S15 runs ETD at 3 to 25 reverse steps, with the distilled EAD at its 8 steps and ESA fixed. The two tables share their default row.
The EAD comparison shows how the activity sampler affects the complete stream. Increasing the number of steps from 2 to 16 brings the generated-to-real count ratio from 0.932 0.932 to 0.996 0.996 , while 32 steps produce a ratio of 1.039 1.039 . CEFS and D count D_{\rm count} improve across the tested settings. Fano error falls from 1.234 to 1.170 even though ETD is fixed, showing that the upstream activity affects the timing statistics of the completed stream. EAD time increases by about 0.16 0.16\, s per step.

在DSEC测试中,这些喷雾在几个步骤的版本上一次不同。 表S14 EAD2至32步的样品,欧空局和ETD固定. 表S15在3至25个反向步骤上运行ETD,其中蒸馏的EAD在8步,欧空局固定. 两表共用其默认行.
EAD比较显示活动采样器如何影响整流. 步骤数从2个增加到16个,使生成与实际的计数比率从0.932 0.932到0.996 0.996,而32个步骤的计数比率为1.039 1.039. CEFS和D计数D_{\rm计数}在测试的设置中改善. 法诺误差从1.234降至1.170,尽管ETD是固定的,表明上游活动影响完成流的计时统计. EAD时间增加约0.160.16\,每步S.

blocks.en: The ETD comparison provides a separate control over the cost of timestamp generation. Increasing the number of steps from 3 to 25 lowers Fano error from 1.359 to 1.119, while ETD runtime rises from 2.8 to 13.1 s per interval. CEFS changes from 0.701 to 0.697 and Same-ts changes by about 0.0002, so the Fano error provides the clearest distinction among these timing settings. The default of six ETD steps balances this timing result with runtime. With the default settings, the few-step pipeline reaches CEFS 0.700 and Fano error 1.217. EventDiffusion-FT at its full settings (Sec. B ) reaches 0.684 and 1.234 on the same windows over three seeds, in about four times the time per interval.

blocks.en:
Table S16 compares three ways of allocating each cell’s events to its pixels. ESA is given each slice’s real cell counts, so only the allocation differs, and ETD times the result as in the pipeline. The even spread places the events uniformly over the cell’s pixels. The binomial split is ESA trained with κ = 1 \kappa=1 in every split (the Conway–Maxwell-binomial of Eq. (5) of the main paper reduced to a binomial), from the same initialization and with the same data and schedule as EventDiffusion-FT’s ESA. The learned dispersion is that ESA. The last row runs the full pipeline, with the distilled EAD’s counts in place of the real ones.
Because every allocation starts from the same real cell counts, this comparison isolates how the events are distributed within cells. On the DSEC test windows, the learned CMB allocation achieves CEFS 0.8035, compared with 0.8029 for the learned binomial split and 0.7997 for the even spread. After ETD assigns timestamps, the completed stream’s Fano error is 1.073 with CMB, compared with 1.118 for the binomial split and 1.116 for the even spread. We also evaluate allocation likelihood separately on held-out gaps from two DSEC test recordings. There, CMB saves 0.134 bits per event over the even spread, compared with 0.080 for the binomial split. These comparisons show how the allocation of a fixed event budget affects spatial fidelity and the timing statistics of the completed stream.

blocks.en:
CEFS complements geometric and feature-based event comparisons. For the
same saved event arrays, the tested RVT-Small, ten-bin adaptation of EQS
scores an empty output at 0.937 0.937 – 0.967 0.967 , while CEFS scores it at zero.
Quantization to 10 ms leaves this EQS adaptation unchanged on all 36
tested pairs, whereas CEFS error increases by 0.838 0.838 – 0.876 0.876 .
These experiments isolate the tested feature representation and do not
claim that every implementation of EQS behaves identically.

blocks.en:
We also compare CEFS structure with PECS Chamfer (CD) and Gaussian (GD)
distances in a separate experiment with seven count-preserving geometric
perturbations and seven reference recordings. Both CEFS
structure and paper-equation CD achieve perfect tested benign-versus-
destructive rank separation (AUC 1 1 ). CEFS’s squared multiscale
structure term has lower benign/destructive error ratios than CD and GD
on these geometric perturbations, while CD remains sensitive to fine point
displacements. In the original PECS evaluation preprocessing, independent
per-stream min–max normalization can erase a global shift or delay:
all 25 physically valid strict alignment tests give CD = 0 =0 although
CEFS responds. A common-coordinate Chamfer implementation also detects
these shifts, identifying the preprocessing choice rather than a universal
limitation of nearest-neighbour distances. Figures S6 – S8 visualize the geometric and timestamp tests. CEFS therefore contributes a
single interpretable score spanning count, signed space–time structure,
and timing, not an across-the-board replacement for specialized metrics.

blocks.en: The duplication experiment tests the activity component. We also evaluate what the other CEFS components contribute. Alongside the unmodified stream, we evaluate random polarity flips (probabilities 0.05 0.05 , 0.2 0.2 and 0.5 0.5 ), rightward spatial shifts (1, 4 and 16 px), timestamp delays (1, 5 and 20 ms), Gaussian timestamp jitter ( 1 1\, ms standard deviation), and timestamp shuffling within 50 ms blocks. We compare the resulting fidelity errors with changes in four downstream tasks: E2VID reconstruction, ESS segmentation, E-RAFT flow and contrast-maximization flow (CMax). E2VID and ESS use our real-event-trained checkpoints. E-RAFT uses its released DSEC-trained checkpoint. These three models are frozen and use temporally aggregated representations. CMax estimates motion using individual event timestamps. Each task receives the same perturbed stream used for the fidelity metrics. To remove the direct contribution of count disagreement, we divide CEFS by its count factor and use one minus this non-count score as the fidelity error. Spatial shifts discard events outside the valid mask, and temporal perturbations can move events across window boundaries, so this is a count-factor ablation rather than an exactly count-matched experiment.
blocks.zh: 重复实验测试了活动成分. 我们还评估欧洲金融共同体中心其他组成部分的贡献。 除了未经修改的溪流外,我们评价随机极性翻转(概率0.05 0.05,0.2 0.2和0.5 0.5),向右的空间转移(1,4和16 px),时间戳延迟(1,5和20 ms),高斯时戳热(1\,ms标准差),以及时间戳在50 mss区块内的洗涤. 我们比较由此产生的忠诚性错误与四个下游任务的变化:E2VID重建,ESS分割,E-RAFT流和对比-最大化流(CMax). E2VID和ESS使用我们经过实际训练的检查站. E-RAFT使用其已释放的经DSEC训练的检查站. 这三种模型被冻结,并按时间汇总表示。 CMax使用单个事件时间戳来估计运动. 每项任务都得到同样用于忠贞度量的扰流。 为了消除计数分歧的直接贡献,我们用计数系数将CEFS除以1减去这个非计数分数作为忠诚误差. 空间移位丢弃有效遮罩外的事件,时间扰动可以将事件移动到窗口边界之外,所以这是一个计数因素衰减,而不是一个精确的计数匹配实验.

blocks.en: For each window we compute Spearman correlation across the selected perturbation conditions, and then average over windows. On CMax, the non-count CEFS error has mean correlation 0.803 0.803 , compared with 0.666 0.666 for PECS-CD, 0.722 0.722 for PECS-GD and 0.371 0.371 for the tested EQS adaptation. CMax degradation is measured against its motion estimates on the corresponding real events, rather than ground-truth flow. The result shows that CEFS’s polarity and space–time components can be informative about a timestamp-dependent task even when its direct count factor is removed. The tested EQS adaptation gives stronger associations on E2VID and E-RAFT, illustrating that learned feature and native-stream comparisons can capture different aspects of downstream behaviour. These selected conditions are a follow-up analysis of 36 windows from nine DSEC recordings. Windows from the same recording are not independent recordings.
blocks.zh: 对于每个窗口,我们计算斯皮尔曼在所选扰动条件下的关联,然后在窗口上计算平均值. 在CMax上,CEFS的误差平均值为0.803 0.803,而PECS-CD的误差为0.666 0.666,PECS-GD的误差为0.722 0.722,测试的EQS适应误差为0.371 0.371。 CMax降解是根据其对相应真实事件的运动估计来测量的,而不是地面真实流动。 结果显示,CEFS的极性与时空组件即使在直接计数因子被移除的情况下,也能了解一个时间戳依赖的任务. 经测试的EQS适应使E2VID和E-RAFT的关联性更强,说明学到的特征和本土-流比较可以捕捉下游行为的不同方面. 这些选定的条件是对9个DSEC录音中的36个窗口的后续分析. 同一录音的Windows不是独立的录音.
